title: Prioritized backpressure SLO and coordinated circuit-breaker policy for multi-region LLM endpoints
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a clear SLO/SLI declaration and an operational policy that ties prioritized backpressure, circuit-breaker hysteresis, and load-shedding to per-endpoint and per-model error budgets across regions. This ticket defines the schema, the orchestration rules for cross-region failover, and the runtime knobs (queue limits, token-budget windows, cache-weighting) required to keep high-priority routes available under bursty load while protecting overall system stability.

Goals:
- Define per-endpoint SLIs (latency P50/P95/P99, availability, generation-quality proxy) with a token-aware normalization so short/long requests are comparable.
- Specify an error-budget accounting model that supports graded priority (customer tiers + route importance) and allows borrowing/repayment semantics across regions.
- Design a coordinated circuit-breaker policy that uses priority-aware thresholds and hysteresis windows to avoid thrashing during flaps.
- Produce a backpressure strategy: request classification, dynamic queue caps, degraded-mode responses (trim + fast-fail vs pass-through to fallback variant), and KV-cache-aware eviction scoring.
- Provide rollout gates and telemetry checks for gradual rollout (canary -> ramp).

Scope and deliverables:
1) SLO declaration template for endpoints and model variants including: SLI names, measurement windows, normalization factors (tokens), severity weight, and default error-budget allocation.
2) Error-budget ledger design: per-route ledger, per-region escrow account, borrowing policy (max percent, repayment window), and priority preemption rules.
3) Circuit-breaker specification: per-variant trip thresholds, latency & error burn coalescing, cooldown/hysteresis parameters, and cross-region inhibition to avoid simultaneous failover storms.
4) Backpressure runtime rules: token-budget sliding windows, queue admission control tied to SLO burn rate, KV-cache impact multiplier for requests with large KV footprints.
5) Simulation harness: traffic generator configs covering multi-region bursts, tenant-weighted load, long-tail sequences; metrics to evaluate SLO burn and failover cascade risk.
6) Operational runbook: alerting thresholds, mitigation steps, manual override knobs, and post-incident analysis checklist.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive early shedding preserves global stability but risks customer-visible degradation for lower-priority tenants. We propose a three-tier degradation ladder with escalating measures (graceful quality reduction -> model variant fallback -> fast-fail).
- Strict token-normalized SLIs reduce bias towards short requests but slightly complicate ingestion and storage. We recommend computing normalized SLIs in the metrics pipeline (pre-aggregated).
- Cross-region borrowing reduces immediate outages for high-priority routes but increases network egress/cost; we limit borrowing to configured regional quotas per release.

Telemetry and gating:
- Primary dashboards: per-route SLO burn, per-region error-budget utilization, circuit-breaker state, and queue depth histograms by tenant and model variant.
- Canary gate: 0% -> 10% -> 50% traffic ramp only if no new 10-minute consecutive burn rate exceedances and circuit tripping rate remains below threshold.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for ledger math and borrowing/repayment logic.
- End-to-end chaos tests with simulated regional outage and burst arrival patterns.
- Load test with KV-cache-heavy traces to validate eviction multiplier effect.

Notes on implementation:
- Metric names will follow naming: redwood.slo.<route>.<sli> and ledger entries will emit redwood.slo.ledger.<route>.<region>.
- Runtime knobs exposed via feature flags: rb.priority_backpressure_v1, rb.cb_hysteresis_v2, rb.kv_eviction_multiplier.

Acceptance criteria:
- SLO template documented and reviewed by PM & SRE.
- Simulator reproduces at least two distinct failure modes with expected mitigation behavior.
- A small canary rollout passes gating checks with zero customer-impact incidents before broader rollout.

2026-02-20 - PM feedback (Lina Nguyen): prefer explicit tenant preemption examples and tie to pricing tiers. Added examples section and updated error-budget max borrow policy.
2026-02-25 - Architecture sync: agreed on token-normalized SLIs and three-tier degradation ladder. Action: engineering to prototype ledger logic (ENG-830002) and SRE to author runbook (ENG-830003).

2026-03-02 - Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1492 - implements ledger arithmetic and basic borrowing API. Code review requested from @sre-team. Failing unit test for repayment window edge-case noted.

2026-03-05 - Simulation results attached in Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b3c/backpressure-sims - initial sim shows acceptable behavior for 95th percentile bursts but exhibits circuit oscillation when regional latency spikes; proposed change to increase hysteresis window to 30s.
2026-03-09 - Design review: added operational override + a metric to track KV-cache write amplification impact. PM approved canary gating strategy pending one more SRE sign-off.
2026-03-10 - Updated ticket to reflect SRE sign-off and bumped estimate for additional integration testing.
